sentence: To find the product \(\log _{n}\left(\frac{1}{2}\right) \log _{n-1}\left(\frac{1}{3}\right) \cdots \log _{2}\left(\frac{1}{n}\right)\) in terms of \(n\), we start by converting each logarithm using the change of base formula.

sentence: Each term \(\log_b \left(\frac{1}{k}\right)\) can be written as \(\frac{\ln \left(\frac{1}{k}\right)}{\ln b} = -\frac{\ln k}{\ln b}\).

Applying this to each term in the product, we get: \[
\prod_{k=2}^{n} \log_{n-k+2} \left(\frac{1}{k}\right) = \prod_{k=2}^{n} \left( -\frac{\ln k}{\ln (n - k + 2)} \right)
\]

This product can be separated into the product of the numerators and the product of the denominators: \[
\left( \prod_{k=2}^{n} -\ln k \right) \div \left( \prod_{m=2}^{n} \ln m \right)
\]

sentence: The numerator is \((-1)^{n-1}\) times the product of \(\ln k\) from \(k=2\) to \(n\), and the denominator is the product of \(\ln m\) from \(m=2\) to \(n\).
